culture.textEn: To make {ko:김밥} (gimbap), you spread rice on {ko:김} (dried seaweed), lay several fillings on it, roll it up and cut it into slices.

sources.title: 김밥 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary entry 김밥, noun)
sources.publisher: 표준국어대사전 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary), National Institute of Korean Language
sources.quoteOrLocator: Entry 김밥 「명사」: “김 위에 밥을 펴 놓고 여러 가지 반찬으로 소를 박아 둘둘 말아 싸서 썰어 먹는 음식.”

sources.title: 김 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary entry 김 3, noun)
sources.publisher: 표준국어대사전 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary), National Institute of Korean Language
sources.quoteOrLocator: Entry 김 3 「명사」 『생명』: “홍조류 보라털과의 조류. … 바닷속 바위에 이끼처럼 붙어 자라는데 식용한다.” (the other headwords 김 1, 2, 4 and 5 are steam, weeds, an occasion and a family name)

verification.notes:
pass 1 (author sourcing, CM-43 S6, 2026-10-30): both Standard Korean Language Dictionary result pages fetched 2026-10-30. Entry 김밥 defines it as food made by spreading rice on 김, putting in a filling of several side dishes, rolling it up and slicing it; entry 김 3 is the red alga that grows on rocks in the sea and is eaten (김 1, 2, 4 and 5 are steam, weeds, an occasion and a family name, so the gloss 'dried seaweed' names sense 3). 'spread rice on' = 김 위에 밥을 펴 놓고; 'several fillings' = 여러 가지 반찬으로 소를 박아; 'roll it up and cut it into slices' = 둘둘 말아 싸서 썰어. Used in: q1 (the recipe card, its Discover sentences) and the q1 Did you know? tip.
pass 2 (MAR culture and facts, 2026-10-30): both entries re-read; the quotes match. Finding fixed: 'a few fillings' said less than the source's 여러 가지 (several), so the note says 'several fillings' (es varios rellenos; ko 속 재료를 몇 가지). The note makes no claim about where gimbap comes from, which sources dispute, and none about 김 farming or regions. The institution is named as on the access date (국립국어원, National Institute of Korean Language). Outcome: fixed.
pass 3 (MAR third pass, 2026-10-30): the recipe card is drawn and generic (no shop, brand or product); its amounts are practice values for two rolls; no Hoya line or caption claims more than the note. Outcome: pass, no change.

culture.textEn: {ko:분식} is food made from flour. From 1962 the Korean government asked people to eat more flour food and mix other grains into rice, to have enough rice, and ramyeon, bread and snacks spread.

sources.title: 분식 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary entry 분식 4, 粉食, noun)
sources.publisher: 표준국어대사전 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary), National Institute of Korean Language
sources.quoteOrLocator: Entry 분식 4 (粉食) 「명사」: “밀가루 따위로 만든 음식을 먹음. 또는 그 음식.”

sources.title: 미곡자급정책, a National Archives theme page on rice self-sufficiency
sources.publisher: 국가기록원 (National Archives of Korea), 기록물로 보는 주제 (theme.archives.go.kr)
sources.quoteOrLocator: “그리하여 1962년 11월, 정부는 ‘혼분식 장려 운동’을 전개하기로 결정하였다.” … “그래서 정부에서는 정책적으로 밀소비를 촉진시키는 이른바 분식 장려 운동을 전개하였다.” … “이러한 분식 장려 운동에 따라 밀가루 소비량이 폭발적으로 늘어났으며, 라면·빵·과자 등의 분식이 많이 생겨났다.”

sources.title: 혼분식 이행 실태, a National Archives theme page in its series 기록물로 다시 살펴보기
sources.publisher: 국가기록원 (National Archives of Korea), 기록물로 보는 주제 (theme.archives.go.kr)
sources.quoteOrLocator: “정부에서는 식량 소비 절약과 자급책의 일환으로 전국적인 혼분식 실천과 음식업소에 대한 단속으로 연간 45만t(약 732억 3,500만 원)의 쌀을 절약하는 성과를 거두고 있는데,”

verification.notes:
pass 1 (author sourcing, CM-43 S6, 2026-10-30): the dictionary entry 분식 4 (粉食, food made from flour, or eating it) and two National Archives of Korea theme pages fetched 2026-10-30. 미곡자급정책 says the government decided in November 1962 to run the 혼분식 장려 운동 (mixing other grains into rice, and flour food), pushed the 분식 장려 운동 harder from 1963, and that flour use grew and flour foods such as 라면, 빵 and 과자 appeared in large numbers; 혼분식 이행 실태 gives saving food and self-sufficiency in rice as the aim. 'From 1962' = 1962년 11월; 'to have enough rice' = 미곡자급, 식량 소비 절약과 자급책; 'ramyeon, bread and snacks spread' = 라면·빵·과자 등의 분식이 많이 생겨났다. Used in: q2 (the snack bar, 분식집) and the q2 Did you know? tip.
pass 2 (MAR culture and facts, 2026-10-30): the three pages re-read; each quote found. Finding fixed: 'the government' became 'the Korean government' (es el gobierno de Corea, ko 한국 정부). The note leaves out the lunchbox checks and the restaurant rules the archive also describes, so it shames no one and stays any-age; it says nothing about how long the campaign lasted or about today's snack bars, which also sell rice dishes such as gimbap. The institutions are named as on the access date (국립국어원; 국가기록원, National Archives of Korea). Outcome: fixed.
pass 3 (MAR third pass, 2026-10-30): the menu and the receipt are drawn and generic (no shop or brand); the prices are round practice amounts; no Hoya line or caption makes a historical claim. Outcome: pass, no change.

culture.textEn: On a food label, {ko:원산지} is the place where the food was produced, and {ko:국산} means it was produced in the country itself, so on a Korean label it means Korea.

sources.title: 원산지 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary entry 원산지, 原産地, noun)
sources.publisher: 표준국어대사전 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary), National Institute of Korean Language

sources.title: 국산 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary entry 국산, 國産, noun)
sources.publisher: 표준국어대사전 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary), National Institute of Korean Language
sources.quoteOrLocator: Entry 국산 (國産) 「명사」: “자기 나라에서 생산함. 또는 그 물건.≒국내산.”

verification.notes:
pass 1 (author sourcing, CM-43 S6, 2026-10-30): the dictionary entries 원산지 (原産地, the place where a thing is produced) and 국산 (國産, produced in one's own country, or such a thing; also 국내산) fetched 2026-10-30. 'the place where the food was produced' = 물건의 생산지; 'produced in the country itself' = 자기 나라에서 생산함. Used in: q3 (the food label, its Check) and the q3 Did you know? tip.
pass 2 (MAR culture and facts, 2026-10-30): both entries re-read; the quotes match. The note states the two word meanings only: it makes no claim about which foods must show an origin, about label law or about grams on a pack, and the drawn label's ten sheets and 2,000 won are practice values. The institution is named as on the access date (국립국어원). Outcome: pass, no change.
pass 3 (MAR third pass, 2026-10-30): the label names no product, maker or brand, and the q3 lines claim nothing about real labels. Outcome: pass, no change.

notes: Volume 2 MAR (row CM-43 S6, F-CURR-002 9.2, 2026-10-30; passes: author, language, culture and facts, learning design, reviser, third pass). No native-speaker or expert review is claimed; language: native-reviewed is the schema's name for the signed-off language gate.

Language pass: spelling, spacing, particles and 해요체 checked line by line (김밥을, 이 김은 국산이에요; 원산지는 ___이에요 and 내용량은 ___이에요, every tile ending in a final consonant); every romanization is the F-CNT-002 converter's (내용량 naeyongnyang). Counters: 장 for sheets, 공기 for bowls of rice, 개 for eggs and a cucumber, with 한, 두, 세 before them.

Language pass (cont.): Applied: the order line's English (One gimbap and one tteokbokki, please); two captions no longer read as speech prompts; es keeps tú for the learner and usted from the server, as Volume 1 does, and says puesto de comida for 분식집; ko questions no longer repeat the key shown under them, and no ko question or Type Hangul prompt writes its answer.

Culture and facts pass: n1 (how gimbap is made) on the Standard Korean Language Dictionary entries 김밥 and 김 3; n2 (분식, and the flour and mixed-grain campaign from 1962) on the entry 분식 4 and two National Archives of Korea pages; n3 (원산지 and 국산) on their entries. Applied: several fillings (the source's 여러 가지), the Korean government. No claim about where gimbap comes from.

Culture and facts pass (cont.): the recipe card, menu, receipt and label are drawn and generic (no shop, maker, product or brand); prices are round practice amounts in won (2,000 to 5,000 on the menu; the receipt's 7,000 is the sum of its two lines); the label's ten sheets and 2,000 won are practice values; no line claims anything about real labels, shops or prices; suits any age.

Learning design pass: 3 quests; new items per quest 6, 6 and 7 (at most 8); Practice and Check items from earlier quests 3 of 7, 6 of 9 and 2 of 4 (lesson-recycle at least 30 in 100), with the Volume 1 words 밥, 달걀, 세 개, 김밥, 떡볶이, 라면 and the prices in new contexts; Checks Type Hangul (Dictation), Realia Read (the receipt) and Cloze Pick (label values), one of each.

Learning design pass (cont.): each Check asks what Practice did not (q1 writes two recipe words by ear after reading amounts; q2 reads the receipt's total and second dish after the menu prices; q3 reads the contents and origin values after the line names, food and price). Triples RR/CP/TH, RR/TR/RR, RR/TH/CP differ from Volume 1's (RR/TH/RR, RR/TR/CP, RR/TR/TH) and from each other.

Learning design pass (cont.): Device voice: prices link 원 to the number (사천 원 [사처눤], 칠천 원 [칠처눤]), and 합계, 국산, 분식집 and 떡볶이 have a tense consonant, so none is in Dictation; the targets 김 and 오이 have no sound change and one spelling each (the meaning dried seaweed settles 김's sense) and play their Type Hangul see fallback while game.type-hangul-hear is at pct 0.
Reviser: applied the fixes above (the order line, the two captions, the ko questions, the es 분식집 wording, several fillings, the Korean government). Third pass: no change.
